answer: The ocean report publishes the merge explicitly at each echo. Each collapsed cluster gets one tide weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, someone who spins up 44 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 278 times the capital for one share. A farm of 1917 identities would post 4384 proofs and burn roughly 67 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
